questions.stem: What are the asymptotes of the graph $y = \frac{3}{x}$?
questions.explanation: For any reciprocal function $y = \frac{a}{x}$, the asymptotes are always the axes: $x = 0$ (the $y$-axis) and $y = 0$ (the $x$-axis).

questions.stem: In which quadrants do the branches of $y = \frac{-2}{x}$ lie?
questions.explanation: When $a < 0$ in $y = \frac{a}{x}$, the branches lie in the 2nd quadrant (top-left) and 4th quadrant (bottom-right).

questions.stem: What is the value of $y$ when $x = 4$ on the graph $y = \frac{8}{x}$?

options.text: Because the result would be negative
Because division by zero is undefined
Because the graph is too steep

questions.explanation: Division by zero is not defined in mathematics. There is no number that, when multiplied by 0, gives 1. This is why the graph has a vertical asymptote at $x = 0$.

questions.stem: The graph of $y = \frac{a}{x}$ passes through $(5, 3)$. What is $a$?
What happens to $y = \frac{1}{x}$ as $x$ becomes very large?
questions.explanation: As $x$ increases, $\frac{1}{x}$ gets smaller and smaller, approaching 0 but never actually reaching it. This is why the $x$-axis is a horizontal asymptote.

questions.stem: How does the graph of $y = \frac{5}{x}$ compare to $y = \frac{1}{x}$?

options.text: It has the same shape but the curves are further from the axes

questions.explanation: Both graphs have the same asymptotes ($x = 0$ and $y = 0$) and lie in the same quadrants (1st and 3rd). Increasing $a$ pushes the branches further from the axes.
